Post natively or via official schedulers (Meta Business Suite planner, TikTok scheduler).
Track any reach drops per account.

Run a split test (or 50/50 traffic by link) and keep the winner by conversion rate and AOV.

how: Add 'fix segment' as the first retry option in qa-check before a full regeneration (our max-3-retries rule).
Describe the region and the fix precisely; re-QA the last frame.
Log credits of edit vs full re-render.

Update price and preview instantly; 'reserve/pre-order' CTA for custom MOQ products.
Measure add-to-cart rate vs a static page.

idea: Keep a named 'elements' library (characters with voice, rooms, product) callable by @name in prompts, and use a micro-expression instruction for multiple emotional beats in one take; still write final shot prompts manually rather than letting the platform agent auto-plan.

Prompt builder replaces @name with the right reference IDs.
Add an optional 'micro-expression beats' line for talking hooks (e.g., annoyed -> surprised -> relieved).

idea: Lock one 'global look' header (camera body, lens, grain, colour grade) and paste it at the start of every Seedance 2.5 prompt so all clips of a product feel shot on the same device.
how: Write a fixed 'iPhone look' block per product (e.g. iPhone 15 Pro main lens, 24mm, slight handheld shake, auto exposure, natural indoor light, no film grain, no cinematic DOF).
Store it as a reusable prompt block in the repo and prepend it to every Seedance/GPT Image prompt.
Add a QA check that compares colour/exposure across clips of one video before delivery.
evidence: Rourke: continuity between shots comes from 'same gear'; he locks '35mm, ARRI Alexa' camera language at the start of every Seedance prompt via Claude, using camera/lens metadata from ShotDeck frames.
source_title: Seedance 2.5 Tutorial: Cinematic AI Video From Start To Finish

idea: Generate one long (~30 s, up to 10,000-character prompt) Seedance 2.5 multi-shot clip and 'mine' the best cuts instead of many separate 5-6 s generations, to get better continuity per credit.
how: For B-roll sequences (e.g. unboxing -> try-on -> reaction) write a time-coded 30 s prompt (0-2s, 2-5s ...) with Claude.
Auto-split the result into shots with scene-cut detection (ffmpeg scene filter / PySceneDetect) and keep only the usable segments.
Track usable-seconds per credit for long vs short generations to decide the default.
evidence: Claim: 30 s generations keep character positions and acting continuity between cuts; short separate clips drift. Seedance prompt max ~10,000 chars; if dialogue speeds up, the script is too long for the duration -> split into two prompts. He uses Premiere 'scene edit detection' to auto-cut.
source_title: Seedance 2.5 Tutorial: Cinematic AI Video From Start To Finish
risk: Long generations cost more per attempt; test on a cheap product first.

Export it as a black-screen MP4 and upload as video reference; in the prompt write 'use @video1 as voice reference of man A'.
Reuse the same voice file for every clip of one 'creator persona' account.

source_title: Seedance 2.5 Tutorial: Cinematic AI Video From Start To Finish

idea: Direct Seedance like an actor: describe micro-expressions, physical surface sounds and a defined character origin/accent in every prompt.
how: Add to our prompt template fields: emotion beats per second, eyebrow/lip/shoulder nuances, what the object lands on (sound), speaker accent/origin.
Give each recurring persona a fixed one-line identity ('woman from Austin, Texas, warm casual tone') reused across clips.
After each generation, dictate time-coded feedback ('at 2s bite lip earlier') to Claude to rewrite the prompt, instead of rewriting manually.
evidence: Rourke: acting nuance is 'the biggest tip'; specifying grass vs concrete changes the impact sound; assigning an accent keeps voice consistent; iterates with Whisper Flow dictation of time-coded notes to Claude.
source_title: Seedance 2.5 Tutorial: Cinematic AI Video From Start To Finish

how: Create .claude/skills/seedance-prompt/SKILL.md with prompt structure (global look, refs mapping @image1/@video1, time-coded beats, audio, negatives).
Include our iPhone-UGC style rules and banned words (brand names that trigger moderation).
Have the production agent always call this skill before any Seedance call.
evidence: Rourke ships a Claude skill 'video prompt builder' that formats prompts with cinematic verbiage and says it is required for good results.
source_title: Seedance 2.5 Tutorial: Cinematic AI Video From Start To Finish

Create a clean 'product sheet' (multiple angles, neutral name) with GPT Image 2.
Log which products got ip_detected so the next run starts from the clean sheet.
evidence: Rourke: a Tamagotchi prop got blocked; removing the word and renaming it 'Pixel Pal' in the product sheet let it through.
source_title: Seedance 2.5 Tutorial: Cinematic AI Video From Start To Finish
risk: Only for our own unbranded products; do not use this to sneak real brands/IP into ads.

A/B one product: graded vs ungraded, compare 3 s retention.
evidence: Rourke always adds a slight Lumetri saturation/exposure lift, same on every clip; says it 'helps significantly' on mobile (claim, no numbers).
source_title: Seedance 2.5 Tutorial: Cinematic AI Video From Start To Finish

Put one real testimonial card directly under the product image (mobile: right after the image).
Add 'see it in action' video block using our own UGC clips and a benefits timeline (week 1/2/3).

risk: Reviews must be real (collected via review app); never fabricate testimonials.

Test direct-to-checkout vs to-cart and track conversion.
evidence: ConversionWise demo: Surge 2.0 allows buttons that add the product and send to checkout or cart from any section; previously required custom code.

Wire external actions through webhooks (Make.com style) where direct API auth is slow.

4-5 -> link to leave a product review (Judge.me/Shopify review app); 1-3 -> support ticket + Slack/Telegram alert to fix the issue.
Auto-reply to every review; personal follow-up to negatives.

Prefer consumables/multi-month products where 2-4 unit bundles make sense.
Compute margin: supplier cost + shipping vs target price (aim >= 3x).

Add shipping option 'Priority insured shipping $4.97' (replacement if lost).
Track AOV and % taking bundle/shipping upsell in the dashboard.

Show margin % trend to catch profit falling as volume grows.

Split big jobs into separate sessions/subagents per task.
